text:
samir: FYI nightly eval 'nightly-v2' hung during quantized sampling on worker-7, took ~6m with repeated heartbeat timeouts then the worker died.

maya: ugh, saw a couple of flakes earlier this week too. any logs?

samir: pasted the tail from the harness below. looks like the sampler got stuck in retry loop and kvcache flush didn't progress.

samir: ```
[2026-03-19T03:12:04Z] eval-harness: starting run id=nightly-v2 model=redwood-q4f
[2026-03-19T03:12:14Z] worker-7: sample_loop entering
[2026-03-19T03:13:00Z] worker-7: heartbeat missed (3/3)
[2026-03-19T03:13:10Z] worker-7: retrying sample chunk idx=42
[2026-03-19T03:15:02Z] worker-7: OOM killed process pid=8123 signal=9
[2026-03-19T03:15:05Z] harness: mark run failed 
```

oliver: does this reproduce locally with the quantized binary? iirc q4f had a mmap path that interacts poorly with our worker pool.

samir: repro is intermittent locally. i can trigger by running the eval subset with --seed 42 but only ~1/6 runs hang.

jen: @ci-bot can you pull the archived core dump and attach the backtrace?

ci-bot: Attached artifact: s3://redwood-ci/nightlies/1855001234/worker-7-core.tar.gz (uploaded) :package: 

maya: notes from a quick glance of the core: threads stuck in function llm::sampler::next_token(), locked on a futex inside the threadpool queue. possible race between sample worker and kvcache eviction.

riley: also saw a very similar pattern last month but it was caused by our temp file cleanup colliding with mmaped quant buckets. are we using per-worker tmp dirs?

samir: harness config for nightlies uses /tmp/eval-run-${RUN_ID} and we rely on auto-clean on exit. worker-7 had /tmp/eval-run-1855001234 still present after the crash. permissions look fine.

oliver: hypothesis: quantized loader maps large tables into memory with MAP_SHARED | MAP_NORESERVE. if eviction tries to munmap from another thread while sampler holds a pointer, you can hit undefined behavior -> hang or crash.

jen: can we add assert checks in the loader to refuse concurrent munmap while active references exist? quick patch in PR could at least fail faster.

maya: also curious about the seed correlation. if sampler RNG path is non-deterministic across threads we may take very different code paths that influence timing.

samir: i've run a bisect: set RNG to deterministic path (single-threaded PRNG) and runs so far (n=18) show 0/18 hangs. with parallel rng (default) 3/18 hang. suggests timing/race amplification.

riley: good find. two-pronged approach: 1) emergency fix -> make loader hold a shared lock until munmap safe; 2) longer term -> harden threadpool shutdown and add per-run resource liveness checks in harness.

oliver: agree. i'll open a small PR to add mprotect + ENFORCE that prevents munmap while active and a debug log when munmap requested. tag: eng-ml/quick-fix.

jen: i'll push a harness change to use per-worker tmpdirs under /dev/shm for nightlies (faster and isolated) and add a preflight that verifies no dangling fds. small PR: harness#428.

samir: repro plan: run nightly subset with --seed 42 on 10 machines with both patches applied, collect logs, and compare failure rate.

maya: also add an eval-case that repeatedly calls sample() with short timeouts to exercise the interaction. make it part of the regression suite.

oliver: FYI i found a small race in threadpool shutdown: submit() can return while worker still holds work item if cancellation wins; PR will add join semantics. hoping for minimal perf impact.

ci-bot: nightly run requeued: job=nightly-v2 retry=1 triggered-by=@samir

samir: thanks everyone. i'll coordinate the run and post results here. feel free to ping if you want to pair on the debug reproducer. :thumbsup:
